```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
devtools::load_all()
results_t1 <- read_csv("../data/results-t1.csv")

n_sim <- 10000

method_colors <- c(
  "z.test.gaussian"      = "#E41A1C",
  "z.test.oracle.kappa"  = "#377EB8",
  "bs.multiplier"        = "#4DAF4A",
  "bs.parametric"        = "#FF7F00",
  "bs.parametric.psd"    = "#0072B2",
  "z.test.null"          = "#984EA3",
  "z.test.null.gaussian" = "#A65628"
)
```

```{R} 
sim_dependent_quadratic <- function(params, method, n_sims=10000){
  set.seed(1)
  map_dbl(1:n_sims, ~{
    hx <- params$h[,1]
    hy <- params$h[,2]
    ex <- rnorm(params$n)
    ey <- (ex^2 - 1) / sqrt(2)
    X <- cbind(hx + ex, hy + ey)

    test.diag(X, method=method)$p.value
  })
}
```

## $p = 2$: Z-Test Methods


## $p = 2$: Null Z-Test $\kappa_{22}$ Estimators

```{r pvals-null}
#| cache: true
#| warning: false
n_vals        <- c(200, 500, 1000)
methods_null  <- c("z.test.null", "z.test.null.regress", "z.test.null.matrix")
method_labels <- c("Z-Test | Null (MoM)", "Z-Test | Null (Regress)", "Z-Test | Null (Matrix)")

pvals_null <- map_dfr(n_vals, \(n) {
  s1 <- scenario(1, n = n, err_type = "normal")
  s2 <- scenario(2, L = 4, n = n, err_type = "exponential")
  map_dfr(seq_along(methods_null), \(j) {
    bind_rows(
      tibble(p_value = pcurve(s1, methods_null[j], n_sim = n_sim),
             method = method_labels[j], n = n, scenario = "Scenario 1"),
      tibble(p_value = pcurve(s2, methods_null[j], n_sim = n_sim),
             method = method_labels[j], n = n, scenario = "Scenario 2")
    )
  })
}) |>
  mutate(
    n      = factor(n, levels = n_vals),
    method = factor(method, levels = method_labels)
  )
```

```{r}
na_tbl <- pvals_null |>
  summarise(
    n_na = sum(is.na(p_value)),
    pct  = mean(is.na(p_value)),
    .by  = c(scenario, method, n)
  ) |>
  filter(n_na > 0) |>
  arrange(scenario, n, method)

if (nrow(na_tbl) > 0) {
  knitr::kable(na_tbl, digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Scenario", "Method", "n", "# NA", "Frac. NA"))
} else {
  cat("No NA p-values across all methods and sample sizes.")
}
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## $p = 2$: Dependence Testing

Correlation dependence testing are closely related but subtly different. In the classical Pearson test, interpretation is dependent on on the assumptions made. 

Consider this canonical example:
$$
\varepsilon_y = \frac{\varepsilon_x^2 - 1}{\sqrt{2}}, \quad 
\varepsilon_x \sim N(0, 1).
$$
Clearly, $\varepsilon_x$ and $\varepsilon_y$ are dependent, but by construction $\operatorname{Cor}(\varepsilon_x, \varepsilon_y) = 0$. Specifically, $\kappa_{22} = 5$. 

Therefore, a dependence test will identify dependence between $\varepsilon_x$ and $\varepsilon_y$, but a correlation test will not. 

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Scenario 1 (Dependent)

```{R dep-test-quadratic-s1}
#| cache: true
#| echo: false

p_cor <- sim_dependent_quadratic(params, method="z.test.null")
p_dep <- sim_dependent_quadratic(params, method="z.test.null.gaussian")
```

```{R}

  "Dependence test"  = p_dep
))
```

### Mechanism: Not in Asymptotic CLT Regime
The u-shaped p-curves indicate that there are insufficient small and large p-values. This means the distribution of bootstrap statistics has less variance than the true distribution. 

::: {.panel-tabset}
## n = 500, p = 10


```{R}
#| echo: false
params <- scenario(1, n = 500, p = 10)
n <- params$n
B <- 1000

# Bootstrap (Parametric)
X <- generate_data(params)
S <- ece_terms(X)
W <- (1 / n^2) * (
  t(S) %*% S +
    t(rotate(S)) %*% S + t(S) %*% rotate(S) +
    t(rotate(S, 2)) %*% S + t(S) %*% rotate(S, 2)
) 
S_bs <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = B, mu = rep(0, ncol(W)), Sigma = W)

# Bootstrap (Oracle)
S_oracle <- map(1:B, ~{
  X <- generate_data(params)  
  S <- ece_terms(X)
  t(colMeans(S)) |> as_tibble()
}) |> list_rbind()
```

```{R}
# Plot Histogram Pair-Plot
col_names <- colnames(S_oracle)
bind_rows(
  as_tibble(S_bs) |> setNames(col_names) |> mutate(source = "bootstrap"),
  S_oracle |> mutate(source = "true")
) |>
  pivot_longer(-source, names_to = "term", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value, fill = source)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)),
                  position = "identity", alpha = 0.5, bins = 20) +
  facet_wrap(~term, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(bootstrap = "red", true = "steelblue")) +
  theme_minimal()
```
